recent_posts.title: Nextra 4 x App Router. What's New and Migration Guide (The Guild)
recent_posts.summary: Nextra 4 introduces significant updates including exclusive support for Next.js App Router with new MDX rendering conventions, Turbopack support for faster bundling, and a switch to the Rust-powered Pagefind for search engine. It also removes theme.config support, necessitating configuration changes. The update optimizes bundle sizes, adds server component i18n support, and enhances components using React Compiler.

recent_posts.title: Understanding the Differences Between GraphQL and REST API Gateways (The Guild)
recent_posts.summary: GraphQL and REST API gateways both serve as intermediaries between clients and backend services, but they differ significantly in their approach and capabilities. REST gateways handle HTTP requests with fixed endpoints, leading to potential data over-fetching or under-fetching. In contrast, GraphQL gateways process complex queries through a single endpoint, facilitating efficient data aggregation and specific data requests. While REST gateways use straightforward caching mechanisms and basic security, GraphQL gateways require sophisticated caching, offer granular security controls, and support schema management directly in code. GraphQL gateways also unify multiple protocols and enhance developer experience, making them a future-proof choice for modern applications.

recent_posts.title: How to write GraphQL resolvers effectively (The Guild)
recent_posts.summary: Resolvers are critical for a robust GraphQL server, handling logic to return appropriate data for each schema field. Key concepts include resolver maps, chains, mappers, and defer resolve, which help optimize database queries and minimize redundant operations. Effective resolver implementation can be improved using tools like GraphQL Code Generator and Server Preset to ensure type safety and reduce runtime errors.

recent_posts.title: Supercharge Your Supergraph with Hive (The Guild)
recent_posts.summary: GraphQL Hive is an open-source platform designed to streamline the management of federated GraphQL supergraphs. It offers tools for schema registry, observability, and collaboration to help handle the complexities of large-scale GraphQL implementations. Hive works seamlessly with Apollo Federation, enhancing developer experience, operational efficiency, and governance through advanced features such as schema validation, performance tracking, and security measures.

recent_posts.title: Introducing GraphQL Mesh v1 and Hive Gateway v1 (The Guild)
recent_posts.summary: The Guild announces the release of GraphQL Mesh v1 and Hive Gateway v1, aimed at enhancing GraphQL Federation with the motto 'Query Anything, Run Anywhere'. GraphQL Mesh allows transforming various APIs into a unified GraphQL schema, compliant with Apollo Federation. Hive Gateway, an open-source GraphQL Gateway, offers seamless integration with multiple schema registries and provides features like GraphQL subscriptions, API usage analytics, and role-based access control. Migration guides are available for existing users, and both tools are designed to be user-friendly and accessible.
